title: Watchlight how-to (long)
note: Script: SmishFilter docs/video/watchlight-howto-script.md. Footage: build 1.0 (14) in the simulator, made-up texts only.

scenes.narration: This is Watchlight, an iPhone app that gives you a second opinion on a text, with its reasons. The check runs on the iPhone, and nothing is sent anywhere unless you share it. Here's how to use it, for yourself or for a parent.
To check a message, press and hold it in Messages and tap Copy. Then open Watchlight and tap Paste.
To see how it works first, tap one of the Try one buttons. Each one checks a made-up example.

From Messages or a mail app, you can also press and hold a link, tap Share, then Watchlight check. Scan a QR code checks a code's link before it opens, and Check a screenshot reads a picture of a message.
Here's a made-up package text. The answer comes first: likely a scam, and what not to do.
Below it, each warning sign has a number. That's how much it counts. The signs add up, and the bar shows the total against the scam line.
Further down, it checks the link and lists what to do, step by step.
When nothing stands out, it says No warning signs found. That isn't a guarantee. If a text asks for money, a code or a quick decision, check with the sender another way.
Ask someone I trust lets you send the text to a person you choose. Report it to seven seven two six starts a text to seven seven two six, which spells SPAM. It's free, and you tap Send yourself.
Already tapped, replied or paid? Tap that button and pick what happened. Do the first step now. Scammers fool careful people every day.
Next, tap the dark card at the top to turn on protection. There are four parts, each under a minute.
The text filter: in Messages, tap the filter button at the top left, then Manage Filtering, and choose Watchlight. Texts from numbers that aren't in your contacts are checked as they arrive.

Caller labels show what a number is known for, from FTC reports. A label isn't proof. The Safari warning speaks up before you type a password into a page pretending to be a company. And with Report on, you can swipe left on a text and tap Report.
Missing a text? Watchlight never deletes texts, and never sorts texts from your contacts. In Messages, look in Junk, and mark the text Not Junk.

Every warning is free. The optional Unlock is a one-time nine ninety-nine. It adds Lock Screen and Siri shortcuts, a saved trusted person and a printable family card. Family Sharing covers the household.
Setting it up for a parent? Do the four steps together, try one example, and tell them they can always send you a text that worries them.
Watchlight. A second opinion on a text, with reasons.
